title: Canadians value in-person third places, but belonging remains constrained by access, cost, time and welcome
source_unit: YMCA Canada and YMCA of Greater Toronto, 2026 YMCA Connections Snapshot
geography: Canada, national survey release; subgroup and provincial comparisons reported in the public summary

denominator.unit: Canadian survey respondents; public release does not disclose the sample size

community_connection.unit: per cent feeling connected to the community where they live all or most of the time

belonging_gap.value: desire for connection remains higher than lived community connection

observations.method: Public summary of the second annual YMCA Connections Snapshot; detailed instrument, weighting, field dates and sample size are not provided in the accessed release.
observations.uncertainty: This is sponsor-commissioned survey evidence with incomplete public methodology; the stable national estimate does not establish causal change or equal belonging across communities.
observations.subgroup: Canadian adults, with provincial and service-access comparisons reported where available.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad belonging question may miss relationships, cultural communities and informal networks that operate outside the respondent's local-community frame; stability may also reflect measurement limits rather than no change.

observations.period: 2026; third places, online connection and face-to-face preference

denominator.unit: Canadian survey respondents; public release does not disclose the sample size

third_place_importance.unit: per cent saying community spaces beyond home and work play an important role in increasing social connection

regular_use.unit: per cent regularly spending time in third places

desired_supply.unit: per cent wishing there were more third places in their communities

online_connection.unit: per cent reporting online connection in 2026, down 5 percentage points from 2025

encounter_route.value: face-to-face experiences rank first among what matters for feeling connected, followed by shared experiences or interests

observations.method: Public summary of survey responses about community spaces, online connection and preferred forms of social connection.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not establish whether limited use reflects supply, affordability, safety, schedule, transport, social anxiety, or selection into other forms of connection; third-place categories are broad.
observations.subgroup: Canadian respondents reporting community, online and in-person connection preferences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low regular use does not necessarily mean spaces are unavailable or ineffective; some people may prefer home-based, workplace, faith-based or culturally specific settings not counted as third places.

observations.period: 2026; barriers to participation in community spaces

denominator.unit: Canadian survey respondents; public release does not disclose the sample size

social_discomfort.unit: per cent naming social anxiety or discomfort as a barrier to community connection

time_barrier.unit: per cent naming lack of time as a barrier

wayfinding_barrier.unit: per cent naming not knowing where to start as a barrier

participation_conversion.value: belonging infrastructure requires social welcome and navigability as well as physical availability

observations.method: Public summary of self-reported barriers to community connection.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not show response overlap, question order, subgroup denominators or whether barriers refer to one preferred program, all community participation, or connection generally.
observations.subgroup: Canadian respondents identifying barriers to connecting with others in their community.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported barriers may describe perceived difficulty rather than actual nonattendance; interventions that solve one barrier may leave time, transport, safety or cultural-fit constraints intact.

denominator.unit: Canadian survey respondents; public release does not disclose the sample size

affordable_programs.unit: per cent saying access to free or affordable programs contributes to belonging

more_use_if_affordable.value: more than half say they would use third places more often if spaces were affordable or free

more_use_if_welcoming.unit: per cent saying they would visit more often if spaces were more welcoming or inclusive

service_access_barriers.value: reported barriers include fitness and wellness programs, mental-health and wellbeing services, children and youth programs, and newcomer and settlement services

institutional_route.value: community organizations can convert belonging demand only when price relief, welcome and usable program pathways are jointly supplied

observations.method: Public summary of perceived contribution of affordability and welcome and barriers to accessing selected community services.
observations.uncertainty: The YMCA's institutional role creates an advocacy and sponsor-framing risk; stated intentions are not observed attendance, durable relationships, or verified community outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Canadian respondents considering community programs, wellness, youth, mental-health and newcomer services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Free access alone may not overcome cultural mismatch, disability access, caregiving, transportation, safety or schedule barriers; program demand may not translate into sustainable provider capacity.

related_sources.claim: YMCA Canada media page confirms the second annual Connections Snapshot release and its national institutional context.
2025 baseline release provides the prior-year comparison and confirms the recurring Connections Snapshot series; it is not used as a 2026 denominator.

boundary: This record adds a community-infrastructure route from desire for connection through third-place supply, affordability, welcome, social confidence, time and navigability to lived belonging. It is a sponsor-commissioned Canadian survey summary with undisclosed sample and incomplete methodology in the accessed release, not a causal evaluation, attendance register, national census of third places, or proof that YMCA provision produces durable belonging.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official YMCA of Greater Toronto 2026 release and YMCA Canada media context were reviewed for the 2025 comparison, belonging, third-place importance and use, online connection, face-to-face preference, barriers, affordability, welcome and service-access findings.
